b_single_provider_error_does_not_stop_lo.actual_error_shape: research/benchmark/mrhbench/executor_broker.py dispatch (except branch): any exception, including ClaudeJSONTransport ProtocolError('Provider safeguard refused the request; ...'), timeouts, structured-output failures and budget exhaustion, becomes {ok:false, error:<type>, message:'Request failed; see your arguments, capabilities and remaining budget.'}; research/benchmark/runtime/container_worker.py rpc raises RuntimeError(answer['message']) and drops the error type. The harness therefore always receives the same RuntimeError text.
b_single_provider_error_does_not_stop_lo.harness_classification: _classify_error (lines 186-206) tests 'budget'/'exhaust'/'quota'/'limit' (line 192) before 'refus'/'safeguard' (line 198); the generic message contains 'budget', so every model failure is kind 'budget'.
b_single_provider_error_does_not_stop_lo.observed: N2_GENERIC_ERROR: first act step raises the real generic error with 29 model calls left -> calls ['act','final'], 28 model calls unused, status partial, omissions [] (no explanation in the manifest). The loop returns at lines 681-683 without consulting budget.remaining().
b_single_provider_error_does_not_stop_lo.contrast: With a typed message ('Provider safeguard refused the request; ...') the harness continues (N2_TYPED_REFUSAL: 4 act steps, tools used, status completed) and stops only after 3 consecutive failures with an omission (N2_THREE_TYPED). A generic error at the final call does get one repair call (N2_FINAL_ERROR). These paths are unreachable on the real worker because the typed text never arrives.
b_single_provider_error_does_not_stop_lo.result: FAIL - reproduces the v1 integration failure class (loop ended on one provider error while budget remained) and contradicts interface v3 model_client.provider_constraints ('One refused call does not mean the budget is exhausted; the remaining budget is reported by budget.remaining()').
b_single_provider_error_does_not_stop_lo.attribution: Primary H0 defect: v3 explicitly told the builder to use budget.remaining(), yet the harness infers budget exhaustion from message keywords. Contributing platform factor: the broker's single generic failure message mentions 'remaining budget' and the worker strips the error type, so no harness can distinguish failure kinds by message. This also explains why the v1 H0 mapped the safeguard refusal to budget_exhausted (its line 360 uses the same keyword rule).

defects.severity: high (functional; affects every task type on the real worker)
defects.location: harness.py lines 186-206 (_classify_error keyword order, 'budget' at 192 before 'refus' at 198) and 679-684 (loop returns on err kind 'budget'); contributing: executor_broker.py dispatch generic message, container_worker.py rpc RuntimeError(message)
defects.finding: Any single model failure (safeguard refusal, timeout, structured-output failure) arrives as the generic broker message containing 'remaining budget', is classified 'budget', and ends the action loop immediately while budget remains. The manifest then says partial with no omission explaining the early stop (only the optional notes artifact records stop_reason). The harness never checks budget.remaining() before concluding exhaustion, contrary to interface v3.

defects.location: harness.py lines 586-605 (context_block: index + notes + run log + recent observations, then text[:180000]); also 581/583 silent [:20000]/[:30000] cuts of ASSETS and OUTPUT CONTRACT in task_block
defects.finding: Truncation removes the tail, which is where recent observations and view_observation output live. Once working notes/index/run log exceed ~180k chars, new tool payloads are never visible (G2). The ASSETS and OUTPUT CONTRACT slices in task_block have no truncation marker.

If the cpu.run hash helper fails, files that scripts modified keep their stale write-time sha and script-created files are not listed; status is correctly partial with an omission. A stale sha would fail controller verify_artifacts (hash_mismatch); the consequence for the stage was not traced.

Any 'R1', 'R2' in EXP content (e.g. 'R2 = 0.91', 'reviewer R1') without that many local runs triggers 'Content references run IDs with no recorded run', which is a status-blocking key (line 970) -> partial.
Real views list 'model_client' and 'asset.read' in tools; both are reported as unknown capability groups in omissions read by the judge. Status unaffected.
Oversized notes: char slicing can yield invalid JSON and does not bound bytes; the broker then rejects the write and the notes artifact silently disappears without an omission.

defects.location: harness.py line 500 (limits from resource_limits/limits only) and task_block 574-584
defects.finding: Real TaskViews carry 'resources' (execution_budget, container cpus/memory/disk, artifact_collection quotas, cutoff/network rules) and 'inputs'; the harness never shows 'resources' to the executor (B2: resources_shown_to_model false). The executor sees only the per-step remaining budget, so collection quotas and container limits must come from the prompt text if at all.
pending_images is cleared before checking whether the model call succeeded; after a failed call the viewed image is never sent (N7), the executor must spend another tool call to re-view.

Because of the same classification, every real tool failure is labelled kind 'budget' in the observation and in omissions (e.g. 'Asset a1 could not be read: budget'), which can mislead the executor and the judge; the original message is kept verbatim alongside.

observations_not_defects: With model_calls <= 2 the harness skips asset pre-reading and produces the final output from asset metadata only (budget-conservative, reported as partial).
cpu.run hash helper uses a fixed timeout 60 (line 913); the broker clips to the remaining wall.
.broker/ reserved paths pass harness path validation; broker rejects them.
Every model request carries the full task block plus up to 4 recent 40k-char observation views; request size up to ~180k chars plus task block.
Status-blocking omission keys include broad substrings 'failed' and 'could not' (conservative toward partial).
Builder self-test for 'no reasoning property' is weak (asserts not (has_reasoning and schema is not SCHEMA)), but the independent scan confirms the property.
comparison_to_v1_H0: Built in one pass with one test-driven fix. v1 defects D1 and D3 are fixed, D4 largely fixed, D2 improved (now partial+omission), D5 and D6 persist. The act schema no longer requests 'reasoning', which removes the specific safeguard trigger of integration v1. However the secondary v1 cause (one provider error treated as budget exhaustion) is reproduced exactly on the real worker, now traced to the generic broker message. Different model/transport context from the sol H0; not a controlled comparison.
verdict_rationale: Interface conformance otherwise holds for all five task types (capability grants, exact manifest shape, model/tool/wall/cancel budgets, malformed output containment, faithful tool payloads, image_id forwarding, state reset, stdlib-only, schemas valid, no reasoning requested). But V3-1 directly violates the v3 disclosed constraint and, with the real worker's error shape, makes any single model failure end the research loop while budget remains; an integration run with this H0 could again measure a platform/harness artifact instead of research behaviour. Per §6/§0.3 maintainers must not patch the H0. Root decision needed: (a) rebuild H0, (b) fix the platform-side ambiguity (broker/worker surfacing a typed failure kind and/or a message that does not mention budget; that is an ABI-visible change for all harnesses and would need a new interface version and re-review), after which this same H0 would take its typed-error path (N2_TYPED_REFUSAL continued correctly), or (c) run integration anyway with V3-1 recorded as a known H0 property and treat any early stop after a provider error as non-measurement. If (b) is chosen and re-verified, the remaining defects V3-2..V3-9 are of the same order as those accepted for v1 and would support development_admissible.
limitations: Fake clients only; no real executor, broker, ContainerExecutor, literature service or research task was run. Nothing here indicates scientific capability; passing self-tests are not acceptance.
Fakes emulate ExecutorBroker/container_worker from source reading; literature payload shapes are approximations.
Real TaskView shapes used without prompt text or asset bytes.
The request object shape {system, messages} was not exercised against the real ClaudeJSONTransport.
Thinking content is empty in the stream; builder reasoning could not be audited. Absence of observed misuse is not proof of role containment (plugins/agents residual context declared).
Consequences of a stale artifact sha for the whole stage (verify_artifacts hash_mismatch) were not traced beyond the broker.
